tagline: A dirt road beside volcanic wilderness and an island of pine
intro: County Road 42 crosses 33 miles of El Malpais National Conservation Area and National Monument, connecting NM 53 with NM 117. The dirt-and-gravel road has blind curves, hills and rugged stretches. BLM presents its Back Country Byway as a route for scenic driving, hiking and wildlife watching. The county routinely grades the surface, but BLM describes sections as rugged and recommends a high-clearance vehicle. Almost all of the route passes through public lands.

The surrounding conservation area was established in 1987 to protect the geological, cultural and wilderness resources of the Zuni-Bandera volcanic field. County Road 42 forms the western boundary of West Malpais Wilderness. The landscape also remains a place of ancestral uses for the Ramah Navajo and Puebloan peoples of Acoma, Laguna and Zuni, including gathering plants and renewing ties to the land.

From NM 53, the road heads south to a Continental Divide Trail trailhead approximately five miles along. The trail winds among the Chain of Craters through piñon, juniper and ponderosa pine. Near the NM 117 end, a side road leads toward the Hole-in-the-Wall trailhead, where a hike crosses plains and lava to a forest island. The drive finishes at the junction with NM 117.

moments.title: Continental Divide Trail
moments.text: A rock cairn marks the Continental Divide Trail across from the northern parking area, approximately five miles south of NM 53 on CR 42. The local section winds among the Chain of Craters, passing piñon, juniper and ponderosa pine. It runs approximately 20 miles between two trailheads on the county road, part of a 3,100-mile route following the continental divide from Mexico to Canada. There are no reliable water sources along this section. At the southern trailhead, approximately nine miles from NM 117, another cairn stands beside the parking area to mark the route.
moments.notice: At the northern trailhead, a rock cairn stands across from the parking area.

moments.title: West Malpais Wilderness
moments.text: Along CR 42, the road marks the western edge of West Malpais Wilderness. Volcanic eruptions shaped its craters, lava tubes, cinder cones and pressure ridges. Congress created the wilderness on December 31, 1987, in the same law that established El Malpais National Monument and the conservation area. Grasses and cacti occupy its open southeastern portion; piñon and juniper grow in western woodlands, with ponderosa pine to the north. Over centuries, wind-deposited material accumulated enough to support plant life on this volcanic ground. The protected area is mostly flat, at elevations from 7,000 to 7,600 feet.

moments.title: Hole-in-the-Wall
moments.text: Hole-in-the-Wall is an island without a shoreline: lava surrounds 6,700 acres of ponderosa pine forest and open rangeland. The geological term is kīpuka, an area of land enclosed by lava flows. Reaching it requires a hike of several miles across open plains and lava. From the NM 117 junction, the approach follows CR 42 northwest for approximately 2.1 miles before a fork leads north for approximately five miles to the trailhead.

practical: West Malpais Wilderness: BLM recommends a high-clearance vehicle for CR 42. The road becomes impassable when wet. Carry water; there is no potable water or restroom along the byway. (checked 2026-10-11)
